This recovery highlights nature's potential when given the opportunity to regenerate naturally.

items.description: The Centre has expanded its crackdown on Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation by delegating powers to state governments. This move allows states to freeze funds and restrict property access associated with the IRF. Following a five-year ban extension on the organization, the home ministry issued a notification detailing these powers. Sections 7 and 8 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act now apply on a state level.

items.title: Ohio lawyer denied partnership wins $2m discrimination award after 9-year suit
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: In a landmark ruling, Pamela Pantages, a lawyer from Ohio, has triumphed in her discrimination lawsuit against her previous employer. The Eighth District Court of Appeals upheld a $2 million jury award, affirming her allegations of being denied partnership due to age and gender bias, as noted in the firm's owner’s comments. This decision corroborates the jury's findings of sex discrimination and contract breaches at The Becker Law Firm.

items.title: Father-son team in South Africa sets 408mph record with 3D-printed drone
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: On December 11, 2025, Mike and Luke Bell shattered records by piloting their Peregreen V4 quadcopter to an astonishing average speed of 408.60 mph, making it the fastest battery-powered quadcopter in history. This remarkable achievement resulted from their dedication to innovative design and rigorous testing, employing advanced aerodynamics and cutting-edge 3D printing techniques. It is a monumental step forward in the realm of drone racing.

items.title: Odisha women turn banana waste into 21,000 festival boats and extra income
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: Odisha's vibrant Boita Bandana festival will witness a creative surge as local women weave miniature boats from banana stems. Supported by around 40 to 50 Self-Help Group members, this innovative project offers a new income stream for the artisans and nearby banana farmers alike. With 21,000 boats on the docket, they're also answering the local government's push to favor eco-friendly materials against plastic options.

items.title: 'He can't be a friend': Zelensky calls Trump's Putin bonhomie 'strange'
items.author: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA
items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky voiced serious concerns regarding US President Donald Trump's close ties with Vladimir Putin, whom he labeled an aggressor resembling Hitler. He expressed disappointment over Trump's positive remarks about Putin while Ukraine faces ongoing conflict. In contrast, Trump described Putin as a friend who genuinely seeks to end the war, revealing the complexities both leaders face in resolving this crisis.

items.description: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' Kansas City Current has extended its impact beyond soccer through community initiatives. The drive helped nearly 400 adults and children in Kansas City, highlighting the organisation's efforts to support local families facing food insecurity beyond the football field.

items.title: Jason Kelce's real estate journey from a $680,000 home to a nearly $6M estate
items.author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
items.description: Jason and Kylie Kelce's Pennsylvania property expansion reflects their changing family needs as they raise four daughters. What began as a $680,000 home has grown into a nearly $6 million estate through multiple neighbouring property purchases. The couple wanted to remain in their existing neighbourhood while creating more space, privacy and security. Despite facing objections from neighbours, their plans highlight their desire to build a comfortable, stable environment for their children.

items.title: 28 ancient Gallic coins found with skull fragments, bronze wagon wheel in France
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Archaeologists exploring Bure in northeastern France uncovered 28 ancient Gallic coins alongside human skull fragments. The site is believed to be a Late Iron Age sanctuary used by the Leuci. In addition to the coins, a miniature bronze wagon wheel was also found, suggesting ritual significance. The discovery contributes to understanding the cultural and religious practices of ancient Gaul. Ongoing studies aim to clarify the site's history and purpose.
